In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AMP deaminase is a highly cooperative allosteric enzyme, which in the liver is regulated by the concentrations of ATP, Pi and GMP, and which is inhibited by GTP.

the AMP deaminase reaction, in the presence of physiological concentrations of substrates and inhibitors, is controlled by the concerted transition theory, with a single equilibrium constant for the transition between two states, one of which is active and the other inactive.

the liver AMP deaminating system, in the presence of physiological concentrations of AMP, Pi and G6P, is controlled by ATP and GTP, the former acting as a positive effector and the latter as a negative one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AMP deaminase is a homodimeric enzyme with one catalytic site per subunit.
